closedNote: Owner graded 7 of 68 and closed the batch: the rest repeat the same pattern (two things tested in the same three or four situations). His notes are written as rules R1-R5 below; they apply to every line made the same way, not only these seven.
rules: R1 Choices name a subject: every conversation choice names a real topic from the records in play (for example 'Ask about the late delivery', 'Mention the council vote'); no subjectless labels such as 'Talk about what is happening here', 'Ask what they would like to do', 'Ask if you can tell them something'. Three or four grounded choices beat seven vague ones.
R2 Leaving is a control, not a line: 'Say goodbye' and 'Let them know you heard' are not conversation choices; the player leaves with the screen's leave control.

R3 A choice answers the last line: the words must fit the other person's last act. A question gets an answer ('Good, how are you?'), an invitation gets a yes or no ('Sure, pull up a chair' / 'Not right now'), a greeting gets a greeting. 'What happened?' after 'How are you?' and 'Good morning' after 'I'd like some company' are failures.

R4 Lines are written for their screen: the day screen is a picture of the calendar and carries no opening sentence; words appear only when something actually happened. Never refer to something the screen does not show ('the list'). People are named by relationship first ('Your sister Emma stayed home sick'). Every grading item shows the screen the line appears on.

R5 Batches cover the whole game: work, home, family, council meeting, campaign door, court, news, journal, Lie lines, personality (the same moment from two opposite temperaments) and the journal story; many places and people, no repeated setups; conversations graded as whole exchanges of several turns with their choices.

R6 Every item is different: no more than two items in a batch share a kind of moment, screen, place, relationship or setup, and the batch is shuffled so neighbors differ. Each item calibrates several things at once (for example register, relationship, temperament, mood, place and screen fit together) rather than one axis, so every grade teaches the engine something new. This replaces the earlier one-axis-per-line batch design.
